---
title: "Training & Mentoring"
---


Training the next generation of scientists is one of the most rewarding aspects of my academic career.

I strive to create a research environment where curiosity, collaboration, scientific excellence, and mutual respect enable students and postdoctoral researchers to develop into independent scholars and future leaders. My mentoring philosophy emphasizes intellectual growth, interdisciplinary thinking, effective communication, and research that contributes to society.

---

## My Mentoring Philosophy

I encourage trainees to:

- Develop strong quantitative and analytical skills.
- Think across disciplines and scales.
- Ask ambitious scientific questions.
- Work collaboratively and respectfully.
- Engage with policy and real-world decision making.
- Communicate science effectively to diverse audiences.

My goal is not simply to supervise research projects, but to help researchers develop the confidence and skills needed for successful and fulfilling careers.

---

## Research Environment

Members of my research group work on topics spanning:

- Climate change impacts on marine ecosystems
- Marine biodiversity conservation
- Fisheries and blue food systems
- Ocean sustainability
- Social-ecological systems
- Future scenarios and tipping points
- Climate adaptation and resilience

The group values collaboration, diversity of perspectives, and mutual support.

---

## Opportunities

I welcome enquiries from highly motivated students and postdoctoral researchers interested in interdisciplinary research at the intersection of ocean science, climate change, biodiversity, and sustainability.

Prospective students should have interests in one or more of:

- Marine ecology
- Climate science
- Fisheries
- Ecological modelling
- Sustainability science
- Quantitative analysis
- Environmental policy

---

## Alumni

Former students and postdoctoral fellows have gone on to careers in:

- Universities
- Government agencies
- International organizations
- Non-governmental organizations
- Environmental consulting
- Industry

Seeing trainees develop into independent scientists and leaders is one of the most rewarding outcomes of academic life.

---

## Working Together

Successful research depends on openness, trust, and shared purpose.

I seek to build a research culture where everyone contributes, learns from one another, and enjoys tackling important scientific questions together.
